html:
SMTO-EXE-0107 — The Gateway's built-in web browser is missing

GUID: 629b754c-4388-52eb-aa73-9be0d92b4534
Slug: browser-browser-binary-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The Gateway has its browser tools, but the Chromium browser program they open isn't installed where they look for it, so SMTO couldn't start a browser for this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, signed in as the account the Gateway runs as, rerun the installer: ./install.sh, or the Gateway installer for Linux, macOS or Windows in the SMTO folder. Chromium is downloaded for one account; installing as a different account puts it where the Gateway can't find it.
  2. Wait until no tasks are running on that Gateway, then restart the Gateway, and restart SMTO too if you used ./install.sh. The Gateway checks for the browser program when it starts.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, and check that its Capabilities now include browser_managed. This confirms the Gateway can now find and start Chromium.
  4. Start a new task for the browsing work. First check whether anything the earlier task did on websites already happened. Tasks already in progress keep the Gateway abilities they started with, and repeating website actions could do them twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's Capabilities list browser_managed, and a new task can open web pages.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details and the installer's on-screen output to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove the Gateway, its pairing or its browser profiles to start over; repairing in place keeps its sign-ins and settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Managed Chromium launch failed with Playwright's "Executable doesn't exist" diagnostic: the Chromium build Playwright expects is not installed for the Gateway's account.

What this means

  • Managed Chromium launch reported the recognized missing-executable diagnostic after the launch effect boundary was entered. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Managed Chromium launch reported the recognized missing-executable diagnostic after the launch effect boundary was entered.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected Gateway's managed browser installation and existing session/profile state before repair; retain the occurrence's effect-unknown flag.

How to fix it

  • As the Gateway's service account, rerun the matching installer (./install.sh, ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1) so Playwright's Chromium is downloaded into that account's browser cache (pw.chromium.executable_path must exist). Restart the Gateway after active work settles, confirm browser.status is ready with browser_managed, and inspect the original attempt's receipts before repeating browser actions.
  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • Chromium launches through the supported managed profile after installation verification and reconciliation of the original attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
